label: text
text: COAL STRIKE OVER.

label: text
text: Loyal Workers' Xmas

label: paragraph_title
text: Windfall

label: text
text: A dejected utterance by Mr. Cook, the miners' secretary, at the conclusion of Saturday's conference. "Men can just drift back any time now" is re-echoed every where as "a true appraisement of the coal stoppage, which is widely considered virtually to have terminated.

label: text
text: Industries are preparing to make up leeway in belated contracts, notably shipbuilding, regarding which the newspapers enumerate contracts for 19 ships of various types lodged with British yards during the past few days.

label: text
text: The Bolsover Colliery Company has announced that in recognition of the loyalty of 2,000 resumed employees in Notts and Derbyshire they are granting a bonus of between 5s. and 12s. a week, according to age. The first installment of this will be designed to be paid a week before Xmas.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: Earlier Messages

label: text
text: A short meeting of the Miners' Executive Committee was held this morning, after which the delegate conference resumed consideration of the Government proposals for a settlement of the dispute.

label: text
text: Two courses are apparently open to the delegates. Either they will accept the responsibility of making a decision or the proposals will be referred to the districts. The moderate section favours the former course, and the likelihood of the districts proceeding at once to make their own settlements independently of the guidance given by the National Federation is a factor which may have an important bearing on the discussion.

label: text
text: Over 8,000 additional miners returned to work yesterday, and many of the leaders are said to fear that further delay might threaten the existence of the Federation.

label: text
text: When the conference adjourned yesterday consultations with the Government were sought to obtain certain elucidations of the proposed terms, and on meeting this morning these explanations were placed before the conference in the form of question and answer.

label: text
text: Broadly, the terms of settlement lay down a standard form of district agreement. An appeal to a national tribunal by either party to a district agreement is provided for in respect of any matter in which that agreement falls short of the standard agreement, provided the length of the working day in the district in which the appeal arises exceeds seven hours.

label: text
text: The proposals are made "contir'gent on an undertaking by the Miners' Federation to promote an immediate resumption of work by means of district settlements in which the length of the working day is not excluded from the negotiations. It is stated that; except in Northumberland, Durham, and one or two of the smaller coal fields, the owners will pay temporarily the rates of wages in force before the stoppage.

label: text
text: Speaking last night, Lord Birkenhead said that, although he could not announce a settlement, he had strong hopes that wise councils would prevail. The Government could draw encouragement in its belief that the terms contained some general principles of justice from the fact that the extremists on both sides repudiated them. The Government had offered the maximum terms now possible and would not hesitate by legislation to implement them if they proved unwelcome to the owners—British Wireless Service.

label: text
text: The miners' conference has decided to refer the Government proposals to the districts with a recommendation for their acceptance.

label: text
text: The card vote on the Miners' Conference decision was 432,000 for the recommendation and 352,000 against it. The Conference by a vote of 427,000 to 357,000 decided for a district vote

label: paragraph_title
text: WORK APLENTY.

label: paragraph_title
text: Once the Coal Strike Ends.

label: paragraph_title
text: MANY BIG CONTRACTS.

label: text
text: 19 New Ships to be

label: text
text:
It is anticipated that when the coal stoppage is over, as it is confidently expected to be when the miners in coulfield give their decisions on the Government's proposals, there will be an immediate and strong revival in the trades which it has rendered more or less idle during the past six months.
The steel and iron works of South Wales have large orders on hand, and many thousands of men will find employment when there is fuel for the furnaces.

label: text
text:
A big firm at Newport has received a contract to supply 22,000 tons of pipe line to San Paulo in South America. This contract will, it is stated, mean employment for British workmen for many years in providing the necessary materials.
In Birmingham iron and steel trade has work of all kinds to put in hand, notably for railway carriages and waggons.

label: text
text: In Sheffield contracts for all classes of steel products have accumulated at an steady increasing rate during the past three months. In shipbuilding, also, arrears of work have accumulated, and the overtaking of these will in itself create a busy period.

label: text
text: Nirteen' new ships and equipment for three more have been ordered in the last few days from various firms.

label: text
text: "Of interest in this connection is the statement made by Mr. Franklin, President of the International Mercantile Marine Company, who arrived at Southampton yesterday from New York."

label: text
text: He said that the White Star Lines are making arrangements to proceed with a big ship, the exact size of which he would not give, beyond stating that it would be larger than the "Olympic". The "Olympic's" tonnage is 46,439.

label: text
text: The new liner will be built by Harland and Wolff, at Belfast, and it is probable the order will be placed in the near future.—British Wireless Service.

label: paragraph_title
text: CHANG KAI-SHEK.

label: paragraph_title
text: ARRIVES AT HANKOW BY PLANE.

label: text
text: Shanghai, Nov. 13.

label: text
text: A message from Hankow reports that the postal workers have struck. The labour unions are more aggressive than ever, paralysing trade. General Chang Kai-shek and Tang Seng-chi have arrived at Wuchang by aeroplane.—Reuter.

label: text
text: [The, above message is specially interesting because it removes all doubt about the Nationalist leader, General Chang Kai-shek, who was reported a fortnight ago to have died from wounds. General Chang is evidently well and in harness again.]

label: text
text: instead of an individual ballot vote. The vote is returnable on the 18th inst. The Conference will re-meet on the 19th inst.

label: text
text: The chief opponents of the Government's coal proposals have been South Wales and Yorkshire, but the recommendation for acceptance is regarded in Government circles as virtually meaning the miners' acceptance of the inevitable and there is the smallest prospect of an adverse vote in the districts.

label: text
text:
Considerable dimiculty is expected in negotiating the district settlements and in any case a general resumption of work is not anticipated for some weeks in many districts.
Sir W. Joyson Hicks stated at Barnstaple that the coal stoppage had nearly ruined the country. It had involved a loss of over £400,000,000 or more than the cost of the South African war. He believed that a Quarter of a million miners had permanently lost employment through the strike.
He declared that if the men were returning with the idea of preparing more strikes it was almost better to fight it out to the bitter end.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: SHAM WAR.

label: paragraph_title
text: Attack on Premiers' Marquee.

label: paragraph_title
text: WONDER VEHICLES.

label: text
text: Good for Roads and Cross Country

label: text
text: The Dominions Premiers yesterday witnessed at. Camberley a wonderful display of the latest forms of tanks and other modern war machines.

label: text
text: There were tanks of every kind, from massive dreadnoughts down to little machines with a crew of one.

label: text
text: There were artillery drugons, roadless tractors, artillery transporters and armoured cars.

label: text
text: was their extraordinary hardness and manoeuvring capabilities. A notable specimen shown was the wheel-comtruck car. A feature of this vehicle is that it proceeds along roads on wheels at the speed of any ordinary motor car and that when cross-country work is necessary a track is substituted.

label: text
text: It takes only one minute to change from wheels to track and vice versa, the change being made by means of engine power in the vehicle itself. Though only in the experimental stage the possibilities of this system of transport are considered to be of the highest importance for the strategy of warfare.

label: text
text: The demonstration concluded with an attack on the marquee in which the Premiers sheltered from heavy rain tanks, tractors, machine-guns, fieldings and aeroplanes co-operating.—British Wireless Service.

label: paragraph_title
text: "ARROGANCE."

label: text
text: CRITICISM OF COOLIDGE'S SPEECH

label: text
text: “The Socialist newspaper “L’Oeuvre” bitterly comments on President Coolidge’s speech in Kansas City, and refers to his “arrogance almost amounting to insolence.”

label: text
text: "L'Avenir" refers to his perfidy and cruelty. It says that ever since the armistice America has played Germany against France.

label: text
text: "Le Journal" is surprised that President "Coolidge's first public utterance since the elections on November 2 should be impregnated with the "bitterness of defeat." The "Figaro" says that the speech reveals American policy to be one of complacent but sensitive isolation with a meticulous regard for "debit and credit " seasoned with tepid altruism."

label: text
text: M. Pertinax. in the "Echo de Paris," says that it would be a big mistake to make an enemy of America, and an equal mistake to expect services from America which she cannot give.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: EMPIRE UNITY.

label: text
text: The members of the Imperial Conference were entertained last night by the Federation of Chambers of Commerce.

label: text
text: Lord Birkenhead said that he believed that by wise and true statecraft in recent years they had surmounted the greatest of the difficulties in the way of closer understanding between Great Britain and the Dominions. The time had come for the complete and common realisation of the only conditions on which an association of communities such as the British Commonwealth could survive, and in attempting to discharge that task they had learned that the qualities which were required were sympathy, knowledge, and imagination. He believed that the Imperial Conference discussions would lead to lasting harmony—British Wireless Service.
